items.note: Mixed-method SEM study of 405 Chinese university students with an experimental (GAI-supported collaborative music creation) versus control group comparison; all listed outcomes (creative interest, creative self-efficacy, self-regulated learning, perceived creative competence) are self-reported, so no scored creative output appears in the abstract; the full text could confirm whether any compositions were rated.

AEA RCT registry entry only (no paper found): within-subject writing task without and then with AI, crossed with randomized incentive arms (flat, piece-rate, tournament), texts scored for originality, grammar and engagement; randomization is of incentive arms, the AI order is not stated as randomized; planned sample 360, no results.

133 Turkish preservice science teachers designed analogies with AI (n = 62) or without AI (n = 71); products coded for format, semantic distance, association type and richness (chi-square tests) rather than rated for creativity; assignment method not stated.

Controlled experiment with 21 industrial design students, AIGC-engaged versus traditional brainstorming, ideas rated on novelty, feasibility, correlation and utility; below 50 participants; abstract read from the Springer landing page (APIs had none).

Design-thinking workshop comparing human-only teams with human-AI teams using the authors' AI ideation app; outcomes are idea counts, usability and novelty of ideas; team-level comparison, sample size and assignment not stated.

Pre- and post-test experiment (N = 300) on AI support for ideation, moderated by creative self-efficacy; abstract says AI enhances creativity but does not say how creativity was measured or how conditions were assigned.

Within-subjects experiment with 75 novice designers on mobile app UI tasks under human-only, exposure to superior AI outputs, and explainable-AI conditions; main outcome is creative self-efficacy, but originality and idea quality are also reported; order randomization not stated.

Architecture studio project at KFUPM with a GenAI test group versus a control group, scored on creativity, time efficiency and design quality (14 percent gain in form and aesthetics); sample size and assignment not stated; also includes expert interviews.

Quasi-experimental pre/post design: 34 interior design students (27 completers) did a manual furniture design then an AI-assisted redesign (Vizcom, Krea.ai, ChatGPT); fixed order, no control group; outcomes are CSI and NASA-TLX self-reports plus expert-juror ratings of designs.

60 engineering students identified design constraints with generative AI or unaided, then all generated concepts without AI (after_ai-type outcome); outcomes are counts of constraints and of sustainability-related concepts plus fNIRS brain activity; no creativity rating stated; assignment not stated.
